summary.name: MacGap
summary.one_liner: MacGap is an Xcode project template that lets HTML/JS/CSS developers build native OS X apps running in a WebView, with a JavaScript API for OS X integration.
keywords: html js css native mac app
wrap web app as mac app
use_cases: build a native OS X app from HTML, JS and CSS
show native notifications from web code
write data to a file from JavaScript in a Mac app
prepare a web-based app for Mac App Store submission
start a lightweight hybrid Mac app project
summary.what_it_does:
MacGap provides an Xcode project that developers use to build OS X apps from HTML, JavaScript and CSS, which run in OS X's WebView using WebKit. It exposes a JavaScript API for OS X integration, such as displaying native notifications or writing data to a file. The page says a blank application weighs less than 1MB. Setup is described as cloning the MacGap2 repository, opening MG.xcodeproj in Xcode, and editing public/index.html to build the app. The page states the API is based on official Apple APIs and is intended to be compatible with Mac App Store submission.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Xcode project template for HTML/JS/CSS apps running in a native WebView
JavaScript API for native notifications and file writing
Blank app under 1MB, per the page
States it is Mac App Store compatible with no embedded chrome browser
caveats: Targets OS X only; the page names no other platforms
Documentation is hosted separately at macgapproject.github.io/documentation
Listed as open source by the GitHub link and Freeware icon in the awesome-mac listing; the page itself does not state a license
